post_content:
Am a bit shaken and terrified both this early in the morning. The reason
being, I read that there was a gangrape just 100 mts near where I stay.
Amazingly, this is the road I take every day not only when I come back from
work late at night after travelling almost 4 h or I go for a good long
solitude walks or a run depending on the need to burn. This wasn't even a
single woman, this woman has been travelling with a guy who was riding the
two-wheeler. It's not like late in the night unless one calls 9 PM late
night!! and above all, I live in Mysuru (Mysore), this is not a place where
rapes are an everyday issue! No, am not ignoring other rapes in other places
and all the glorified versions of it. But am concerned about women safety!
Worse, I just crossed the street at 830 PM yesterday after a long and tiring
day! Might be, I was not in two-wheelers and I did have a driver to drive
around, but then this woman also had somebody driving her? What are we doing
about woman safety? who is taking this seriously? okay, somebody told me all
women should learn martial arts! I am an expert in Karate, but does that mean
I can kick 5 men in inebriated state? after putting in about 10 h at work, do
I have that physical strength to fight? hashtag#life hashtag#challenges

profile_headline: I help YOU to build YOUR brand on LinkedIn | YOU=Startups+People | Host of Podcast: Demystifying LinkedIn | #demystifyLI
post_content:
Point at your readers if you want to get their attention on your
hashtag#LinkedIn posts! Yes, you read it right 🙄 It's not offensive! In real
world, pointing at someone may not be a good etiquette. In writing world,
pointing at your readers with your words is a good technique to make your
content stand out. There's following paragraph, "When we write content, we've
to put focus on our readers to make them get connected with our content. As
it's not about us. It's about our readers." Now read following paragraph.
"When you write content, you've to put focus on your readers to make them get
connected with your content. As it's not about you. It's about your
requirements readers." Do you observe the difference? 🤔 In first example,
writer is talking about herself. She's putting focus on herself. Whereas, in
second example writer is talking about YOU. You are her readers. By using the
word "you" instead of "I" and "we", she put the whole focus on her readers.
Wherever you put your focus, determines the attention you would bring 🧐 By
using YOU, the writer is grabbing attention of her readers which is the heart
and soul of EFFECTIVE writing. Use YOU instead of I and WE to make your
readers feel important. That's the key! 😁 What do you use? You or I/We?
